budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the commission had to vote on dividing a spending limit for the timber rights fund between purchase of service and supplies for fiscal year 2026, using a spreadsheet supplied by the finance office.
A commissioner recommended most of the fund go to supplies rather than services since trail maintenance work is done mostly in-house.
The commission voted by roll call to allocate the fund as proposed between supplies and purchase of service.
A commissioner reported a reimbursement request had been submitted for engineering, design and permitting work at two trail sites, with the reimbursement expected to cover most of what was spent.

budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner described an Eagle Scout project at the pollinator habitat that added a rain barrel system, funded entirely through the scout's own fundraising.
A commissioner serving on the stormwater task force said the proposed town stormwater utility fee was projected to raise this much per year from residents and businesses.

budget_items.topic: Proposed stormwater utility fee per household

The administrator was directed to upload DEP comment emails into OpenGov going forward so all commissioners can see them.

390 Howard Street will be continued to July 16, with the office told to tell the applicant that failure to appear with an updated survey/wetland flag plan could result in the commission voting to deny for lack of action.
The chair will follow up with the office on whether the town or the original applicant should request the certificate of compliance for the 452 boulder installation, since it is now town property.

The office will be asked to correct the agenda for 167 Towns and Harbor Road, since the application appears to involve removal of about 19 trees rather than the 3 dead trees listed, which may require reclassifying it from a determination to an RDA.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission welcomed two new commissioners, worked through a full docket of wetland hearings, and discovered mid-meeting that a hearing on a deck/sunroom project had never been properly noticed to abutters, forcing it to restart. The board also voted to split its small FY2026 timber rights fund between supplies and services, heard updates on trail grants and the pollinator habitat, got a briefing on a proposed town stormwater utility fee, and said goodbye to its departing interim administrator, Sophie.

what_happened.line: A hearing on a deck and sunroom addition at 833 Flatville Road was found invalid for lack of abutter notice and must be reopened from the start.
The commission continued three other hearings, including one on Howard Street with a warning that continued applicant inaction could lead to denial.
The commission voted to split its FY2026 timber rights fund between supplies and purchase of service.

A discrepancy was flagged in a Towns and Harbor Road tree-removal application, where the number of trees described in the record did not match the agenda listing, and the office was asked to correct it and possibly reclassify the filing.
The commission received a briefing on a proposed town stormwater utility fee that would charge residential and commercial properties.

why_it_matters: The abutter-notice failure means neighbors near 833 Flatville Road get a fresh chance to be heard before that project can proceed, and the applicant's timeline is delayed.
The timber rights fund vote is a small piece of the commission's FY2026 budget, split between materials and outside services for trail work.
The stormwater utility fee, if adopted, would appear as a new recurring charge on residential and business bills; the commission only heard a briefing and took no vote on it.
